name: Sharp X68000
description: A Japanese 16-bit home computer launched by Sharp in 1987. Its sprite hardware, FM sound and high-resolution graphics made it close to the arcade boards of its time, and it received faithful ports of many arcade games. It never sold outside Japan.

specs.graphics: Up to 768 × 512; 65,536 colours at lower resolutions; hardware sprites
specs.sound: Yamaha YM2151 FM (8 channels) + OKI MSM6258 ADPCM

curiosities: Its twin-tower case, with a fold-out carry handle, earned it the nickname "Manhattan".
Its YM2151 sound chip is the same one used in many arcade boards of the era.
It ran Human68k, a disk operating system modelled on MS-DOS.
Its last direct successor, the 1993 X68030, moved to a Motorola 68EC030 processor.
